narrative.overview: SimplySync is rendered as a signal system an engineer can inspect. Railway interlocking diagrams, packet traces, equipment labels, and control-room indexes provide the grammar: hard routes, explicit nodes, numbered sections, visible state, and no ornamental containers. The product mechanism—not decorative chrome—is the memorable image.
keyCharacteristics: hard-line diagrams and explicit junctions rather than card stacks
cool equipment fields with carbon ink and semantic signal colors
system sans for reading and tabular monospace for machine notation
numbered indexes with visible current position
square controls, flat panels, and zero decorative elevation

rules.name: The Signal Must Mean Something Rule
rules.body: Saturated color may encode action, route state, warning, success, or focus. It may not decorate a section.

rules.name: The Dual Board Rule
rules.body: Dark mode changes the board field and signal luminance, not the system's hierarchy or geometry.

rules.name: The Two Instruments Rule
rules.body: Every text role is either prose or notation; no third decorative type voice is introduced.

rules.name: The Control Board Is Flat Rule
rules.body: Ordinary content never floats and never uses ambient card shadows.

dos: Do let diagrams, counters, IDs, and real code carry visual interest.
Do expose device, relay, encryption, and ownership boundaries explicitly.
Do vary density: a concentrated trace earns a quiet reading field.
Do preserve state meaning and geometry across light and dark themes.
donts: Don't use an oversized generic headline above a row of equal feature cards.
Don't wrap every idea in a rounded rectangle.
Don't add gradients, glows, glass, grain, blobs, or decorative dashboard chrome.
Don't turn the interlocking grammar into train illustration or nostalgia; it remains functional notation.
